records.quote: Theorem 20 For i = 1, 2, ..., n, let Ui ~ GM(alpha_i, beta_i, lambda_i) and Vi ~ GM(alpha*_i, beta_i, lambda_i). Further, let Ii (Ii*) be a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of Ui's (Vi's) with E(Ii) = p_i (E(Ii*) = p*_i), i = 1, 2, ..., n. Then, if alpha, alpha* in D+ (E+), beta in D+ and prod_{i=1}^n p_i >= (<=) prod_{i=1}^n p*_i, alpha >=^m alpha* implies X_{1:n} <=hr (>=hr) Y_{1:n}.

records.quote: Theorem 7 Let {X1, X2, ..., Xn} and {Y1, Y2, ..., Yn} be two sets of independent random variables each following the multiple-outlier GM model such that Xi ~ GM(alpha_1, beta_1, lambda_1) and Yi ~ GM(alpha*_1, beta_1, lambda_1), for i = 1, 2, ..., n1, and Xi ~ GM(alpha_2, beta_2, lambda_2) and Yi ~ GM(alpha*_2, beta_2, lambda_2), for i = n1+1, ..., n1+n2 = n. Then, alpha_1 <= (>=) alpha_2, beta_1 >= beta_2 and (alpha_1,...,alpha_1,alpha_2,...,alpha_2) >=^m (alpha*_1,...,alpha*_1,alpha*_2,...,alpha*_2) implies X_{1:n} <=_{R-hr} (>=_{R-hr}) Y_{1:n}.
records.family: multiple-outlier Gompertz-Makeham model, n1 + n2 = n
records.compared: outlier-alpha vectors under majorization, two-group configurations

hypotheses.formal: (alpha_1 x n1, alpha_2 x n2) >=^m (alpha*_1 x n1, alpha*_2 x n2)

conclusion.order: ageing: R-hr (relative hazard-rate ageing; r_{1:n}(x)/s_{1:n}(x) decreasing)
conclusion.direction: X_{1:n} <=_{R-hr} Y_{1:n}, i.e. hazard-rate ratio r_{1:n}(x)/s_{1:n}(x) decreasing in x

records.ambiguity: R-hr is the paper's relative-ageing order (X <=_{R-hr} Y iff r_X(x)/s_Y(x) decreasing); not plain hazard-rate order.
